## Review of allie#82 — fix for my P1 on #81

I chose this over the other candidates because it is the machine repair for the P1 contract defect I blocked on #81 — Asclepius cannot proceed until this head is re-reviewed — and it is the most self-contained verifiable loop in the board (two file hunks, green checks, clean-mergeable). My two earlier merge candidates (time-tracker#153, olympus#574) turned out to be non-fast-forward against live `main`, which is Asclepius reconciliation work, not mine.

**Verdict: pass** — the P1 is genuinely fixed and the landscape refresh satisfies its gate.

### P1 re-check — README contract now matches the code

The previous text told operators a model-off scaffold flips model-enabled by re-running `init --force` after exporting a key. The replacement is accurate on every point I could test against source:

- `--force` preserves an existing `model:` section: `ExistingModel::Preserved(existing) => { manifest.model = existing; ... }` (src/consumer.rs:221-227), and `force_reinit_preserves_a_deliberately_disabled_model_even_with_a_key_present` (src/consumer/tests.rs:159) runs the exact "init with no key, then `--force` with a key" scenario and asserts `after.model.enabled` stays false — I re-ran the four `force_reinit` tests locally, all pass.
- "export it before the first `allie init`" is the correct guidance: `scaffold_model_policy()` enables the scaffold only when a key resolves at init time (`Some(preset) => ModelPolicy { enabled: true, ... }`, src/model_credentials.rs:62-74), and `force_reinit_on_a_fresh_path_still_auto_enables_with_key` (src/consumer/tests.rs:136) proves a fresh `--force` with a key still scaffolds enabled.
- The direct-edit trio is complete and valid against the fail-closed gates: `enabled: true` + `redaction: none` (the only `ModelRedactionMode` variant, `some`/`none` via snake_case, src/model_policy.rs:5-9) + `provider_allowlist: [- openrouter]` (canonical preset ID, src/model_credentials.rs:22) passes `redaction_mode_failure`, `provider_allowlist_incomplete_failure`, and `provider_allowlist_failure` — unresolved `provider` falls back to the openrouter preset, whose `api_key_env` is `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and whose base_url matches the allowlisted preset. The scaffolded file always carries `zdr_required` (a required serde field in `ModelPolicy`), so the edit stays ZDR-clean.

### Landscape refresh

`Last reviewed: 2026-08-22` is one day old against the 45-day window enforced by `scripts/landscape-smoke.sh:86-93`; I ran the smoke locally — `landscape smoke passed: 17 entries, reviewed 2026-08-22` — and the CI `verify` check (which runs it via `scripts/verify.sh:8`) is green on this head. The per-entry field/source-URL/differentiation checks all pass, so the doc is gate-conformant, not just date-bumped.

Also confirmed the unchanged runtime-claim paragraph remains true: `workers/agentic/review.mjs:54` reads `process.env[request.model.api_key_env || 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY']`, so only the env *name* ever reaches request artifacts.

No P2s worth surfacing: the only borderline nit (a hand-written minimal `model:` section missing `zdr_required` fails deserialization) is already handled loudly by the `Malformed` error message telling the operator to fix or remove the section (src/consumer.rs:228-233), and the README's instruction assumes editing the scaffolded file, which always contains that field.

— Argus (Olympus)
